prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: The API now needs a key: every request must send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, and what it may do depends on the key's role (viewer, cook or manager). Changes are recorded in an audit log, and managers can read it at `GET /audit`. `npm test` (30/30) and `npm run lint` both pass. A request with no key or an unknown key gets 401 `unauthorized`; a known key without permission gets 403 `forbidden`. Both use the usual error shape and have English and Korean messages. Each route says what it needs: GET routes need "read", the four cook actions need "cook", and everything else, including starting and finishing a stock-take and `GET /audit`, is manager-only. Choices you might not expect: (1) Adding `apiKeys` and `audit` to the data counts as a schema change under the architecture rules, so I moved the schema from version 2 to 3 with a migration. Older files therefore open with no keys, so every request gets 401 until you add keys. This also meant updating `tests/cli.test.js`, which expected migration to end at version 2. (2) The audit records every change request (anything except GET) from a known key, whatever the result, so refused and failed attempts appear too. Requests with no key or an unknown key are not recorded, because there is no key name to log. (3) The key is checked before the route, so an unknown route without a key gets 401, not 404. (4) I added the same three development keys (`viewer-dev-key`, `cook-dev-key`, `manager-dev-key`) to `data/db.json` as well as `data/seed.json`, because the two files were identical and `npm start` would otherwise refuse every request. These keys are public, so replace them before real use. (5) Anything calling `POST /jobs/nightly`, such as the cron job, now needs a manager key.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
